paper.title: Better Algorithms for Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions

unmapped: Corruption level C = sum_t ||R~^t - R^t||_inf is unknown to the learner; bounds depend on its realized value
Adversary observes current stochastic rewards before corrupting but not the player's current choice
settings.definition_quote: A stochastic reward $\rew^t_i \in [0,1]$ is drawn for each arm $i$ from its reward distribution; The adversary observes the vector $\rew^t$ and generates corrupted rewards $\wt{\rew}^t \in [0,1]^K$; The player picks $i_t \in [K]$, possibly at random, and observes the corrupted reward ... $C = \sum_{t=1}^T \norm{\wt{\rew}^t - \rew^t}_\infty$.

algorithms.name: BARBAR (Bandit Algorithm with Robustness: Bad Arms get Recourse)

conditions: C is the realized corruption level, unknown to the learner

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \cref{alg:barbar} is bounded by \[ O\Bigg(KC + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{\log{T}}{\Delta_i} \log\!\Big(\frac{K}{\delta}\log{T}\Big) \!\Bigg). \]

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret sum_t(mu* - mu_{i_t}) with high probability. Paper also remarks (informally) that with delta=1/T the expected regret is O(K E[C] + sum 1/Delta_i log^2(KT)); Appendix B shows an Omega(KC) instance for BARBAR; Section 5 sketches an informal Omega(C) lower bound for any algorithm and improved O~(C + sum 1/Delta_i) bounds under extra assumptions (not recorded as formal results).

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandits with adversarial corruption of total level C (unknown)
